item.text: {"question_id":"1B.4","answer":"During 2023, the DRC remained party to the Pelindaba Treaty, NPT safeguards and Additional Protocol, TPNW, and CTBT, and the IAEA records acceptance of AFRA on 27 September 2023. UNODA also records receipt of the DRC’s TPNW Article 2 declaration on 25 April 2023. These establish state-level nonproliferation and restraint commitments, but the supplied records do not identify Tshisekedi’s personal role or demonstrate 2023 funding, inspections, implementation, enforcement, or compliance. In the broader de-escalation sphere, the government and MONUSCO co-signed a note on 21 November 2023 containing an accelerated, gradual, orderly, and responsible withdrawal plan, with transition arrangements intended to support civilian protection, disarmament, security-sector reform, justice, and criminal-justice capacity; the evidence does not establish completion or outcomes, and Tshisekedi did not personally sign the note. Countervailing evidence shows that Tshisekedi’s government rejected political dialogue with M23, adopted a hardline stance toward the EAC force, and ended its mandate after disputed results; the EAC record also reports competing interpretations, external actors, and no measurable security improvement. His administration separately requested accelerated MONUSCO withdrawal, creating unresolved protection risks, although the formal disengagement plan provides contrary evidence of an orderly and responsible process. Overall, the evidence supports inherited and some contemporaneous state-level commitments plus formal de-escalation planning, but does not establish personally directed treaty implementation or consistently effective compliance during the 2023 period.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0017-E004","BATCH-0023-E019","BATCH-0024-E001","BATCH-0028-E002","BATCH-0026-E002","BATCH-0010-E007","BATCH-0025-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E016","BATCH-0011-E017","BATCH-0010-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most nuclear-treaty evidence concerns inherited DRC state status rather than a ruler-attributed 2023 choice.","The TPNW declaration is recorded as received on 25 April 2023, but the supplied passage does not establish who submitted it or Tshisekedi’s role.","No supplied passage documents 2023 nuclear inspections, funding, enforcement, compliance, disarmament implementation, or treaty violations.","The MONUSCO plan describes intended arrangements rather than completed withdrawal outcomes or durable civilian-protection capacity.","Regional-force outcomes reflect M23, Rwanda, other regional actors, competing mandates, and disputed interpretations; causal attribution to Tshisekedi alone is limited."] ,"corrections_made":["Separated inherited treaty status from target-period ruler conduct.","Added the dated 2023 TPNW declaration as a distinct state action while preserving uncertainty about personal attribution.","Added the formal MONUSCO disengagement plan and its stated civilian-protection, disarmament, reform, and justice components.","Preserved contrary evidence concerning rejection of M23 dialogue, EAC mandate disputes, accelerated MONUSCO withdrawal, and unresolved security risks.","Removed unsupported implication that treaty participation demonstrated personal implementation, funding, inspection, or compliance."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full ledger review would be warranted if primary records identify Tshisekedi’s role in the 2023 TPNW declaration or AFRA acceptance.","Further evidence of 2023 safeguards implementation, inspections, funding, compliance, or MONUSCO transition outcomes could materially change the assessment."]}
